title: GenAI evaluation evidence
summary: Audit programme for generative AI systems: tool logs ingested and recomputed by the engine, readiness-gated conclusions on accuracy, attacks, leakage, agents, harmful content and Art. 50 transparency, mapped to the OWASP LLM and Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS and the AI Act.

controlObjectives.statement: Assess whether the GenAI test plan, the run metadata and the validation of model-graded judges were fixed before the evidence was ingested and are sufficient for the conclusions drawn.

addresses.justification: Art. 9(8) asks for testing against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds; the frozen plan and its floors are that definition for GenAI tests. Testing covers more than GenAI evaluation.

items.title: GenAI test plan, metadata and judge validation
items.objective: Assess whether the GenAI test plan, the required run metadata and the validation of model-graded judges are sufficient before any GenAI conclusion. Supporting evidence; the auditor determines sufficiency. Claim scope: benchmark accuracy is not accuracy on the population of real inputs, and a low attack-success rate holds only for that attack set, configuration and judge.

procedures.text: Approve the plan: criteria, bands, primary scores, minimums and judge-validation floors (kappa lower bound at least 0.60 on at least 50 items; plans may raise, never lower them, D-10 and D-16).
Declare the bundle: system snapshot and developer-level family, decoding, tools with permissions, dataset and judges with their families.
Review the metadata checklist of every run and obtain missing fields before ingestion.
Validate each model-graded judge with a bound human-label file from a different model family than the system under test.
Have a reviewer acknowledge post-run edits, tool-aggregate mismatches, declaration and family conflicts and deterministic declarations.

items.signOffGate: Independent reviewer clears blocking notes and approves the exact revision; the GenAI readiness gate (genai-evidence design section 12.3) must show no blockers before a supported or qualified conclusion.

items.title: Accuracy, hallucination and benchmark scope
items.objective: Assess task accuracy and the rate of unsupported statements on declared benchmarks. Supporting evidence; the auditor determines sufficiency. Claim scope: benchmark accuracy is not accuracy on the population of real inputs, and a low attack-success rate holds only for that attack set, configuration and judge.

procedures.text: Freeze the plan before ingestion, declare the bundle of accepted tool logs and ingest it through the enrolled worker; an uploaded envelope counts as L1 until a worker recomputation matches it.
Read the recomputed members (n, estimate, interval, p-value) per run and the reconciliation with the tool's own aggregates; never re-score or execute anything a log names.
Check the benchmark's relevance to the intended purpose and the declared accuracy levels; record contamination and saturation risks.
Record the engine's claim-scope statements in the results and state which population, attack set, configuration and judge the conclusion covers.

items.signOffGate: Independent reviewer clears blocking notes and approves the exact revision; the GenAI readiness gate (genai-evidence design section 12.3) must show no blockers before a supported or qualified conclusion.

procedures.text: Freeze the plan before ingestion, declare the bundle of accepted tool logs and ingest it through the enrolled worker; an uploaded envelope counts as L1 until a worker recomputation matches it.

items.title: Transparency to users (Art. 50)
items.objective: Supply recomputed evidence on AI-interaction disclosure and on marking and detection of synthetic outputs to the Art. 50 papers WP-XC-07, WP-XC-10 and WP-XC-12 of the AI Act pack, which hold the Art. 50 conclusions (A50-ED-32). Supporting evidence; the auditor determines sufficiency. Claim scope: benchmark accuracy is not accuracy on the population of real inputs, and a low attack-success rate holds only for that attack set, configuration and judge.

procedures.text: Freeze the plan before ingestion, declare the bundle of accepted tool logs and ingest it through the enrolled worker; an uploaded envelope counts as L1 until a worker recomputation matches it.
Read the marking criteria (marking presence, detection rate, false-positive rate, detection after transformation, self-identification rate) with their Wilson intervals per pre-registered stratum.
Record that signature verdicts in marking records are as the provider's validator reported them; the platform does not verify signatures yet.
Cross-reference the result in the Art. 50 papers instead of concluding on Art. 50 here.
Record the engine's claim-scope statements in the results and state which population, attack set, configuration and judge the conclusion covers.

defaults.coverageRule: Unknown, not_run, inconclusive and error do not count as pass.
defaults.statement: GenAI evaluation evidence supports an audit assessment and does not constitute legal compliance, a conformity certificate or a security guarantee.

reporting.limitations: Assurance conclusions do not constitute a notified-body conformity assessment, legal certification or a security guarantee. GenAI conclusions rest on tool logs recomputed by the platform's engine: benchmark accuracy is not accuracy on the population of real inputs, and a low attack-success rate holds only for the attack set, configuration and judge tested.

notes: Pack for #33 (docs/design/genai-evidence.md sections 9.4 and 12.4); 2026.11.1 (#145) adds MITRE ATLAS v2026.10 links and changes nothing else.
